Key names are string literals repeated across read/merge/apply/restore functions.

issues.summary: GPUtil is unmaintained and only used for GPU discovery
issues.suggestion: Remove GPUtil and parse nvidia-smi/psutil directly, or adopt pynvml if a library is required; this drops an unmaintained dependency.
evidence: pyproject declares GPUtil>=1.4.0.
GPUtil imports distutils spawn.find_executable, which is deprecated on Python 3.14.
gpu_monitor.py already shells out to nvidia-smi for the primary path.

issues.summary: Two package cycles increase import-order fragility
issues.suggestion: Break the cycles by moving shared types to leaf modules and keeping package __init__ files free of re-exports.
evidence: The cycles detector reports cli/__init__ <-> cli/main and engine <-> checkpoint.
Both pairs are initialized during normal package imports.

issues.summary: CLI command bodies mix parsing, preflight, orchestration and rendering
issues.suggestion: Extract one function per phase (prepare, execute, persist, render) and keep the command body as a short composition; pass a small prepared-context object instead of a dozen locals.
evidence: optimize and auto are each 603 lines; _auto is 402 and _display_optimization_result is 362.
Each body performs several side-effecting phases sequentially with shared local state.

issues.summary: Report generation is one 531-line function with many inline formatting branches
issues.suggestion: Split into section builders that each return lines, then compose them in save_best_report; this keeps formatting testable without changing output.
evidence: save_best_report builds every section (header, config table, quality, ladder, presets, diagnostics) in one body.
Section formatting is interleaved with data lookup and fallback handling.

issues.summary: Async functions perform blocking work without awaits
issues.suggestion: Move blocking repository/file work to asyncio.to_thread or a background task where it can delay the event loop; keep pure in-memory work inline.
evidence: Several async handlers call synchronous repository/file helpers directly.
Long CPU-bound preparation runs on the event loop instead of a thread.

issues.summary: Settings cross the CLI/API -> optimizer -> benchmark boundaries as an untyped dict
issues.suggestion: Define one AdvancedSettings model at the outer boundary, validate once, and pass it through; remove per-layer .get default logic.
evidence: prepare_run/execute accept advanced_settings: dict.
Each layer reads different keys and applies its own defaults.

issues.summary: BenchmarkService wiring is duplicated between CLI and API
issues.suggestion: Create a factory (build_benchmark_service(settings)) in services and call it from both entrypoints so defaults and flags cannot diverge.
evidence: Both entrypoints construct BenchmarkService and translate settings into config fields.
The two argument lists drifted, which required a dedicated parity fix.

issues.summary: API response mapping is split between converters and dict enrichment
issues.suggestion: Move enrichment into the schema/converter or a single presenter function, and return one response shape per resource.
evidence: _convert_config_result builds a schema, then _enrich_config_detail mutates its dict form with extra keys.
Different endpoints apply different subsets of enrichment.

issues.summary: Legacy engine and checkpoint modules have no direct tests
issues.suggestion: Either add characterization tests before deleting them, or remove the legacy stack and its imports so the critical untested surface disappears.
evidence: The scan lists both as critical_untested with 3 importers.
They are the compatibility path for ui/web.py and are still imported during test collection.

issues.summary: Two test roots with different conventions obscure the canonical suite
issues.suggestion: Consolidate into tests/ by domain, or document and enforce the split with pytest markers (unit vs integration) and a CI matrix.
evidence: testpaths includes both roots.
Fixture setup and import style differ between them.

issues.summary: Server-load and host-lifecycle paths are covered only by fakes
issues.suggestion: Add httpx.MockTransport-based contract tests for the LM Studio and Ollama clients covering timeout, 4xx/5xx and malformed payloads.
evidence: Load-response loss and echo-probe failures required new fallback tests after live findings.
Most coverage uses monkeypatched clients rather than a fake HTTP transport.

issues.summary: Most API handlers return untyped dicts instead of response models
issues.suggestion: Add response_model (or typed return annotations) to every public handler and move inline dict construction into schemas/presenters.
evidence: Only 12 of 62 @router handlers set response_model.
Handlers such as list_models, get_status and get_runs build dicts inline.

issues.summary: Routes are re-registered manually at import time in api/main.py
issues.suggestion: Pin the FastAPI version that works, use include_router normally, and add a startup assertion that the expected route count/prefixes exist.
evidence: Comments at lines 63-106 describe recreating routes because include_router failed.
The workaround duplicates APIRoute handling and makes route ownership hard to follow.

issues.summary: Similar endpoints mix sync and async handlers
issues.suggestion: Standardize on async handlers for I/O endpoints and use def only for purely CPU-bound short handlers; document the rule.
evidence: Some handlers are async def, others are def, including endpoints that perform the same repository/file work.
Blocking work in async handlers can stall the event loop.

issues.summary: No API route enforces or documents an authentication boundary
issues.suggestion: Either add a local API token (generated at startup, required by mutating routes) or document the localhost-only threat model and enforce it with a startup host check that refuses non-loopback binds.
evidence: route_auth_coverage reports 0 authenticated handlers out of 62 in routes.py and 11 in main.py.
State-changing endpoints include /apply, /runs/{id}/save-default and /runs/{id}/delete.

issues.summary: Localhost binding is the only access control and is not enforced at startup
issues.suggestion: Add a startup check: if host is not loopback and no API token is configured, refuse to start or require an explicit allow-remote flag.
evidence: config.web_ui.host defaults to 127.0.0.1 but can be overridden by environment.
No startup guard rejects a non-loopback host or warns about unauthenticated exposure.

issues.summary: State-changing actions are not audit-logged
issues.suggestion: Log a structured audit event (action, model, run id, old/new config hash) for every apply/restore/save-default operation.
evidence: Apply/restore/save-default endpoints mutate LM Studio and Ollama configuration files.
There is no record of which run or caller triggered the change.

issues.summary: Defensive broad catches hide failures in service code
issues.suggestion: Replace copied catches with one logged best-effort helper and let unexpected exceptions propagate; keep only documented tolerances.
evidence: optimizer.py contains 41 'except ...: pass' blocks, many around optional enrichment/persistence.
The pattern is copied across modules rather than centralized.

issues.summary: Print statements remain in service modules
issues.suggestion: Use logger.info/debug with structured fields and let the CLI render user-facing output.
evidence: optimizer.py prints during long runs, bypassing structured logging.
community_benchmarks.py and deepresearch.py print progress from service code.

issues.summary: Docstrings on long functions describe only one responsibility
issues.suggestion: Either split the function so the docstring is accurate, or expand the docstring to list all side effects and outputs.
evidence: save_best_report is documented as saving a report but also builds diagnostics, presets and ladder sections.
_test_config documents loading but also benchmarks, scores and cleans up.

issues.summary: Deprecated ui/web.py and its legacy engine/checkpoint/client dependencies remain active
issues.suggestion: Delete ui/web.py, optimizer/engine.py and storage/checkpoint.py after migrating their three importers; keep a release note for 2.0.
evidence: ui/web.py is marked DEPRECATED but defines a second FastAPI app and 8 routes.
It imports optimizer.engine, api.client, benchmark.runner and storage.checkpoint.
engine.py is explicitly kept for backward compatibility with ui/web.py.

issues.summary: discovery/inspector.py still uses the legacy api/client instead of the service client
issues.suggestion: Port inspector.py to the service client and delete api/client.py once tests stop importing it.
evidence: inspector.py imports LMStudioClient, LoadConfig and ModelInfo from api.client.
The current host client lives in services/lm_studio.py.

issues.summary: Legacy benchmark/runner.py coexists with services/benchmark.py
issues.suggestion: Move the remaining test to the service API and delete benchmark/runner.py with the legacy engine.
evidence: runner.py defines BenchmarkRunner/BenchmarkResult and is imported by engine.py and one test.
services/benchmark.py is the active benchmark implementation.

issues.summary: Hardware scripts sit at the repository root instead of with the hardware package or tools
issues.suggestion: Move them under tools/ (or lm_optimizer/hardware/) and update entrypoints/README references.
evidence: Both root files have low fan-in and import lm_optimizer.services/domain.
The hardware package already owns detection and monitoring.

issues.summary: services/ is a flat directory mixing unrelated capabilities
issues.suggestion: Split into capability subpackages and keep a small services/__init__ facade for compatibility.
evidence: The directory contains orchestration, benchmark execution, reporting, host defaults, sandboxing and recommendation logic.
There are no subpackages to signal ownership.

issues.summary: tools/ mixes durable utilities with one-off campaign scripts
issues.suggestion: Move one-off scripts to tools/archive/ with a README, and rename durable tools by action (validate_live.py, audit_webui.py).
evidence: 39 scripts include reusable probes (live_validation, webui_audit) and dated campaign slices (speed16k_part2, speed16k_remaining_rerun).
No README or naming rule distinguishes them.

issues.summary: API routes keep current optimizer/run in module-level globals
issues.suggestion: Move current-run state into app.state or a small RunRegistry created in the lifespan hook and injected via dependency.
evidence: _current_optimizer and _current_run_id are assigned inside request handlers and read by later requests.
The scan reports 5 mutations of module-level state in this file.

issues.summary: Logging setup performs filesystem I/O at import time
issues.suggestion: Make logging configuration explicit in the app/CLI entrypoint (lifespan or main) and keep the module import side-effect free.
evidence: logging_config imports config and setup_logging() creates config.storage.logs_dir.mkdir(...).
Any module importing logging_config can trigger directory creation before the app starts.

issues.summary: api/main.py rewrites the route table at import time
issues.suggestion: Use a supported include_router pattern, move optional routers into a registration function called from the lifespan hook, and assert the final route table in a test.
evidence: Lines 63-106 manually recreate and filter APIRoutes because include_router was reported broken.
Late imports inside the module add hidden initialization order.

issues.summary: Command functions own several distinct responsibilities
issues.suggestion: Extract a shared optimization workflow service and keep CLI commands as thin adapters that parse input and render results.
evidence: optimize/auto combine argument validation, preflight, host lifecycle, run execution and report rendering.
The same responsibilities are also implemented in the API path.

issues.summary: _test_config combines load, benchmark, quality and persistence
issues.suggestion: Split into load_candidate, measure_candidate, evaluate_candidate and record_candidate steps composed by _test_config.
evidence: The 244-line function loads a model, runs cases, evaluates quality, records results and cleans up in one body.
Failure handling for each stage is interleaved.

issues.summary: Two checkpoint/persistence implementations serve the same lifecycle
issues.suggestion: Delete the legacy CheckpointManager with the legacy engine and keep one checkpoint contract.
evidence: storage/checkpoint.py is the legacy CheckpointManager used by the legacy engine.
storage/run_checkpoint.py is the active checkpoint store used by the adaptive optimizer.

issues.summary: save_failed_report uses None for two different outcomes
issues.suggestion: Return a small result object or raise/return distinct sentinels (e.g. Skipped(reason)), or document the ambiguity and add an explicit has_winner check at call sites.
evidence: The function returns None when a best config exists and when there are no configurations.
Callers treat None as 'nothing to save' without knowing why.

issues.summary: Public helpers annotated -> dict return different key sets by branch
issues.suggestion: Return Pydantic models or TypedDicts with required/optional fields, and keep raw dicts only at serialization boundaries.
evidence: Several handlers and default helpers return dict with optional keys added conditionally.
Callers use .get(...) because the annotation does not promise a shape.

issues.summary: Docstrings describe the happy path but omit raised errors
issues.suggestion: Add Raises/Returns sections for public functions and align annotations with every return path.
evidence: save_failed_report says 'Returns path' but can return None.
Client methods raise on transport errors without a documented Raises section.

issues.summary: Retry and fallback branches repeat load/benchmark logic with slightly different guards
issues.suggestion: Extract a single attempt function returning an outcome and drive retries from one loop with an explicit retry policy.
evidence: LM Studio load fallback checks response, then polls loaded instances, then re-raises with a different message.
Benchmark reasoning fallback runs the same case twice with a conditional keep.

issues.summary: Long functions make the success condition hard to locate
issues.suggestion: Extract a small is_successful(run) predicate and use it at each decision point; keep rendering separate from decision logic.
evidence: The command bodies and report builder have several early returns and nested conditionals spread over hundreds of lines.
A reader must scan the whole body to know when a run is considered successful.

issues.summary: Some async functions perform no awaits
issues.suggestion: Convert purely synchronous handlers to def, or add a real await (e.g. asyncio.to_thread) for blocking work.
evidence: Several async handlers only call synchronous repository/template helpers.
They could be plain def handlers, which would let FastAPI run them in a threadpool.

issues.summary: Most service parameters and returns lack annotations
issues.suggestion: Annotate public entrypoints first (prepare_run, execute, run_cases, auto_run) with concrete types and enable mypy/pyright on those modules to prevent regression.
evidence: The AST census finds 693 unannotated parameters and 264 unannotated returns.
Public service methods accept advanced settings and config fragments as bare dicts.

issues.summary: dict[str, Any] is used where a concrete shape is known
issues.suggestion: Define TypedDicts (or dataclasses) for the LM Studio defaults document, duel payload and host guard state; keep Any only for genuinely dynamic JSON.
evidence: lmstudio_defaults.py has 23 dict[str, Any] annotations for a JSON document with known keys.
Key strings are repeated across merge/apply/diff functions.

issues.summary: type: ignore comments lack error codes and explanations
issues.suggestion: Use '# type: ignore[code]  # reason' and fix the underlying narrowing issue where possible.
evidence: 12 of 20 ignore comments are in normalization.py.
Most use bare '# type: ignore' without the suppressed error code.

issues.summary: Raw string literals bypass phase/stage/status enums
issues.suggestion: Normalize input once into enum members (parse_phase_skips) and compare enums internally; keep strings only at CLI/JSON boundaries.
evidence: The enum bypass census reports 30 comparisons against raw strings.
Skip-phase handling compares strings such as 'quality' instead of OptimizationPhase members in places.

add.description: backends/base.py defines BackendClient and assert_conforms, and OllamaClient implements the seam; backend-specific code is not spread through the domain.
web_main.py launches api.main:app, and ui/web.py is explicitly marked as deprecated reference code, so the current entrypoint is unambiguous.
The deprecated ui/web.py docstring names api.main:app as authoritative, which prevents a new engineer from wiring the wrong app.
OptimizationPhase/OptimizationStage enumerate the pipeline stages instead of relying on implicit string flow, which gives the orchestration a readable spine.
1,666 detected names across all packages use snake_case, so lexical convention is not a source of friction.
Most test modules are named after the production module they cover, which makes coverage discovery predictable.
BenchmarkService records success=False and an error per case instead of aborting the whole sweep, which keeps one bad prompt from losing a run.
Cancellation paths explicitly checkpoint state before unwinding, preserving recoverability across failures.
Terms such as run, configuration, phase, winner and ladder are used consistently across CLI, API and services, so domain names transfer between layers.
The BackendClient protocol is implemented by OllamaClient and exercised by conformance checks, so the abstraction has more than one consumer.
Functions such as parse_phase_skips and compose_granular_skips encode real skip semantics rather than forwarding arguments.
One HTTP client (httpx), one settings stack (pydantic-settings) and one CLI/UI stack (Typer/Rich + FastAPI) avoid duplicate-purpose libraries.
Helpers such as _looks_incomplete, _sample_mem and _extract_mtp_metrics are short, side-effect-light and easy to test.
The optimizer exposes ordered phases and skip names, so the CLI/API handoff for phase control is at least named and testable.
About 1,490 tests run in roughly five minutes, covering phases, scoring, persistence and CLI/UI parity.

add.header: Targeted regression tests for live findings
add.description: Load-response loss, echo-probe cleanup and context-speed ladder retries each gained a dedicated test after being found live.
Run, settings, compare, sandbox and judge endpoints use Pydantic response models, giving the most important payloads a stable schema.
The web UI binds 127.0.0.1 by default and CORS allows only localhost origins, reducing accidental network exposure.
The 2.5% comment ratio and short docstrings avoid restating code; comments generally explain constraints or intent.
web_main.py launches api.main:app and the deprecated module points to it, so the target of the migration is unambiguous.
domain, storage, backends, benchmark and scoring are named by responsibility, so the main layout is self-explanatory.
pydantic-settings provides one typed config object with environment support, avoiding scattered os.environ reads in most modules.
The FastAPI app uses a lifespan context for startup/shutdown work, giving a clear place for future initialization.
AdaptiveOptimizer runs named phases (speed, context speed, quality, recovery, validation) with explicit skip handling, which is a coherent orchestration spine.
Core domain dataclasses expose to_dict/from_dict pairs and are exercised by round-trip tests, giving persistence a reliable contract.
CLI and API helpers commonly validate inputs and return/raise early, keeping the happy path visible in short functions.
Domain dataclasses and Pydantic schemas type the main entities (runs, configs, metrics, requests), giving the persistence and HTTP layers a reliable core.
